Maya (PM): Heads-up — acme wants a zero-downtime upgrade contract for their on-prem deployment. They specifically asked for an in-place patch path without node reboots and a signed rollback plan. Anyone seen this before?
Ravi (Eng): We don't have a true zero-downtime upgrade for on‑prem today. Dedicated supports rolling upgrades, but our current onprem packaging requires agent restarts or node replacements. :thinking:
Jen (Solutions): Acme also expects SSO + HSM rotation windows — they will only permit changes in a 2-hour maintenance window monthly. That constraint is going to drive the approach.
Luis (CS): They also flagged a security requirement: 30-day patch SLA and a signed rollback runbook. Customer said they'd budget to pay for development effort if we ship a hotpatch/handoff flow.
Tom (Infra): Hotpatching the runtime is tough because of model/kv-cache compatibility. A more pragmatic option: route traffic to a temporary fallback (hosted or dedicated) during upgrades so customer sees no downtime. That needs customer-managed networking support (NAT changes, DNS TTL, or SRV routing).
Maya (PM): Framing options for the roadmap discussion: A) Contractual SLO: scheduled 2-hour maintenance windows + detailed migration playbook (low eng work, higher ops for customer), B) Invest in a rollback + prefetch agent flow to enable in-place upgrades with minimal traffic loss (medium dev effort), C) Offer a paid "upgrade-assist" service where Redwood provisions a short-lived hosted fallback and handles the cutover (fastest to market). Thoughts?
Claire (Security): Option B requires immediate threat modeling. Prefetching model artifacts onto customer infra could violate airgap/controls unless explicitly allowed. Need opt-in and additional controls (encryption at rest, attestations).
Jen (Solutions): From field economics, C looks easiest short-term. We already have hosted routing and routing policies; adding a documented assisted upgrade play is mostly process + SRE time. Legal will need precise language for liability.
Ravi (Eng): Rough estimates: B (prefetch + safe rollback) is a 6–8 sprint prototype and 4–6 quarter full product. C (hosted fallback + managed cutover) is ~2–3 sprints to wire the routing, canary tooling, and docs. A is mostly PM/docs/legal.
Maya (PM): Great. Proposed next steps and owners: 1) Legal to draft contract addendum for option C (Maya to assign), 2) Eng to kick a routing-fallback spike and canary script (Ravi), 3) CS to validate acme will accept scheduled maintenance windows if C is delayed (Luis). I will loop in Sales for commercial terms.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: routing-fallback-spike (link: https://internal.re/infra/1967890123)
Luis (CS): I'll confirm acme's willingness to accept the assisted service vs in-place expectation in tomorrow call. :white_check_mark:
Ravi (Eng): Starting spike tomorrow morning, will post findings to /eng-runtime and attach perf numbers and rollback proof-of-concept.
Maya (PM): Thanks — keeping this thread as canonical for the customer's upgrade ask and our roadmap decision. Please post status updates here by EOD Friday so we can decide in next roadmap sync.
